content.value_statement: Scheduling events by hand can miss required Google Calendar options. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through safe gws calendar event creation.
actual_capabilities: Shows the required gws calendar +insert arguments for event title, start time, and end time.
Documents optional calendar ID, location, description, attendee, and Google Meet settings.
Uses RFC3339 or ISO 8601 time formats for calendar event start and end values.
Points users to shared Google Workspace authentication and global flag guidance.
Warns agents to confirm with the user before running the write command.
limitations: Requires the gws CLI and an authenticated Google Workspace account.
Only documents event creation, not updates, deletions, recurring events, or reminders.
Does not check calendar conflicts or attendee availability before creating an event.
Creates real calendar events, so execution needs explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Schedule Team Meetings
use_cases.description: Create calendar events with titles, times, attendees, and optional Meet links after confirming the details.

use_cases.title: Prepare Executive Calendar Entries
use_cases.description: Build clear event requests with location, description, and calendar selection for busy schedules.

use_cases.title: Automate Workspace Scheduling
use_cases.description: Use a repeatable CLI workflow to add Google Calendar events from operational tasks or support requests.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Event
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner event creation with required fields only.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a Google Calendar event named [title] from [start time] to [end time]. Confirm the details before running any write command.

prompt_templates.title: Add Event Details
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate event creation with optional fields.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a calendar event for [calendar] with title [title], time [start] to [end], location [location], and description [description]. Ask for missing required details.

prompt_templates.title: Invite Attendees and Add Meet
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced scheduling with attendees and video conferencing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Google Calendar event for [title] with attendees [emails] and a Google Meet link. Confirm attendee addresses, timezone, start time, and end time first.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Full Event Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow that checks readiness before execution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this event request: [details]. Normalize times to RFC3339, identify missing fields, confirm the final event plan, then create it only after approval.

output_examples.input: Schedule a Standup tomorrow from 9:00 to 9:30 with a Meet link.
output_examples.output: I will confirm the date, timezone, and calendar, then create the Standup event with a Google Meet link after approval.

output_examples.input: Add a Review meeting with Alice on the team calendar next Tuesday afternoon.
output_examples.output: I need the exact start time, end time, timezone, and Alice email address before creating the event on the team calendar.

output_examples.input: Create a planning session with location and description.
output_examples.output: I will prepare the event title, time range, location, and description for confirmation before making the calendar change.

best_practices: Confirm the calendar, title, timezone, start time, and end time before creating the event.
Use RFC3339 or ISO 8601 timestamps to avoid ambiguous calendar times.
Review attendee emails, locations, descriptions, and Meet settings with the user.
anti_patterns: Running the write command before the user explicitly confirms the event details.
Using vague times such as morning or afternoon without a timezone and exact range.
Adding attendees, descriptions, or Meet links that the user did not request.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It helps create new Google Calendar events through the gws calendar +insert workflow.

faq.question: Does it require Google Workspace access?
faq.answer: Yes. The gws CLI must be installed and authenticated for the target Google Workspace account.

faq.question: Can it add attendees?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented attendee option can be used multiple times for invited email addresses.

faq.question: Can it add a Google Meet link?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented Meet option adds a Google Meet video conference link to the event.

faq.question: Does it update existing events?
faq.answer: No. This skill covers creating new events only, not updating or deleting existing events.

faq.question: Should the command run automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that this write command should be confirmed with the user before execution.
